note.text:
Look at the expression 5x + 3y − 7.
• The variables are the letters, x and y: they stand for numbers that can change.
• The terms are the parts joined by + and −: 5x, 3y and −7. The sign in front belongs to the term.
• A coefficient is the number in front of a letter: the coefficient of x is 5 and the coefficient of y is 3.
• The constant term has no letter: here it is −7.
Hidden ones: in x − y + 4, the coefficient of x is 1 (x = 1x) and the coefficient of y is −1 (−y = −1y).

worked_example.problem: For the expression {poly([a, 'x'], [b, 'y'], [one, 'z'], [c, ''])}, name the variables, the terms, each coefficient and the constant term.
steps: The variables are the letters: x, y and z.
The coefficients: {a} for x, {b} for y, and {one} for z (z = {one}z).
The constant term is the term with no letter: {c}.
worked_example.answer: Variables x, y, z; coefficients {a}, {b}, {one}; constant term {c}.

cards.idea: The variables of an expression are its letters.
example: In {poly([a, 'x'], [b, 'y'], [c, ''])}, the variables are x and y.

check.prompt: Which are the variables in {poly([a, V[0]], [b, V[1]], [c, ''])}?

misconceptions.explain: {a} and {b} are the coefficients, the numbers in front of the letters.
{c} is the constant term: it has no letter.
Those are terms. The variables are just the letters.

cards.idea: Terms are the parts of an expression joined by + and −. The sign in front belongs to the term.
The coefficient of a letter is the number in front of it, with its sign. x has coefficient {one} and −x has coefficient −{one}.
example: In {poly([a, 'x'], [b, 'y'])}: the coefficient of x is {a}, of y is {b}.
In {poly([one, 'x'], [-one, 'y'])}: the coefficient of x is {one}, of y is {-one}.

cards.idea: The constant term has no letter. Keep its sign.

questions.prompt: How many terms are there in {poly([a, 'x'], [b, 'y'], [d, 'z'], [c, ''])}?

misconceptions.explain: Count every part joined by + or −, including the constant term.

solution: The terms are the parts joined by + and −.

questions.prompt: What is the coefficient of {V[1]} in {poly([a, V[0]], [b, V[1]], [c, ''])}?

misconceptions.explain: Keep the sign in front of the term: {mono(b, V[1])}.

solution: The coefficient is the number in front of {V[1]}, with its sign.

questions.prompt: What is the constant term of {poly([a, V[0]], [b, V[1]], [c, ''])}?

misconceptions.explain: Keep the sign in front of the number: the constant term is {c}.
{a} is a coefficient; the constant term has no letter.

solution: The constant term is the term with no letter, with its sign.

questions.prompt: Which expression has coefficient of x equal to {k} and constant term {c}?

misconceptions.explain: The coefficient goes in front of x and the constant term stands alone.
The constant term is {c}: check its sign.
The coefficient of x is {k}: check its sign.

solution: The coefficient of x is the number in front of x: {mono(k, 'x')}.

questions.prompt: What is the coefficient of {V[0]} in {poly([b, V[1]], [s, V[0]], [c, ''])}?

misconceptions.explain: There is a term with {V[0]}, so the coefficient is not {z}: {mono(s, V[0])} = {s}{V[0]}.
Keep the sign in front of the term.

solution: {mono(s, V[0])} means {s} × {V[0]}: a letter on its own has coefficient {one}, with the sign in front of it.
